title: Blood brothers: WHO chief joins ENHYPEN to celebrate drive success
keyFacts: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) is a self-confessed fan of K-pop sensation ENHYPEN and this week, he got the chance to tell them so in person.

title: West Bank: Guterres alarmed as Israel imposes sweeping closures after deadly Hebron attack
keyFacts: The UN said on Friday it was “extremely alarmed” by intensifying violence in the occupied West Bank, as Israel moved to seal off the territory following a deadly attack on its soldiers in Hebron.

title: Sudan: Drone strikes killed at least 306 people in three weeks
keyFacts: UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Friday strongly condemned an escalation in drone strikes across Sudan this month, which killed at least 306 people and injured hundreds more in the first three weeks of October alone.

title: Soil mapping aims to boost agricultural production in Kenya
keyFacts: A new Kenyan initiative is helping farmers better understand their soils in a bid to improve crop yields amid intensifying climate shocks.

title: ‘Burden and loss’ builds in DR Congo, as Kenya strengthens Ebola containment
keyFacts: As Ebola continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), more resources are needed to fight the disease and feed patients and families, UN agencies said on Friday.

title: Yemen: Deepening concerns for Taiz City as aid is blocked from entering
keyFacts: Aid agencies warned on Friday of the fast-developing humanitarian emergency inside Taiz City in Yemen, which has been encircled by de facto Houthi forces fighting government troops along the country’s west coast.

title: World News in Brief: Russian attacks intensify, UN team tours West Bank, ‘unlawful’ elderly deaths
keyFacts: Long-range Russian attacks across Ukraine are intensifying, including in Kyiv, causing at least 14 civilian deaths and 78 injuries overnight into Thursday, as UN agencies continue to provide aid.

title: First human case of Shamonda virus reported in France as patient dies
keyFacts: A patient in France has died after being infected with Shamonda virus, the first recorded human case of the disease.

title: Nepal’s deadly glacier flood a ‘defining moment’ for the international community
keyFacts: The deadly flash flood that tore through Nepal in August is a “defining moment” for both the country and the international community, according to the head of the UN field agency which builds roads, schools and clinics in crisis zones.
